name: Baron Samedit (CVE-2021-3156) - Sudo Heap Overflow
description: Baron Samedit exploits a heap buffer overflow in sudo (versions 1.8.2 through 1.8.31p2 and 1.9.0 through 1.9.5p1) via sudoedit -s. It grants instant root without needing any credentials or sudo permissions. One of the most impactful Linux privesc CVEs - affects nearly every Linux distribution released before January 2021.
notes:
=== CHECK IF VULNERABLE ===
  sudoedit -s /
  # Vulnerable: starts with "sudoedit:" (error message)
  # Patched: starts with "usage:" (normal usage message)
  # Or check version:
  sudo --version
  # Vulnerable: 1.8.2 - 1.8.31p2, 1.9.0 - 1.9.5p1

=== EXPLOIT (multiple variants) ===
  # Python NSS variant (most reliable):
  git clone https://github.com/worawit/CVE-2021-3156
  cd CVE-2021-3156
  python3 exploit_nss.py
  # Root shell!

  # C variant:
  gcc exploit.c -o exploit
  ./exploit

=== AFFECTED DISTROS ===
- Ubuntu 20.04 (Focal) - default install
- Debian 10 (Buster)
- CentOS 7/8
- Fedora 33
- Nearly all Linux distros pre-Jan 2021

=== THE BUG ===
sudoedit -s triggers a heap buffer overflow when processing
backslash-escaped characters. The overflow can overwrite
service_user struct to load attacker-controlled shared library.

recommended.note: LES identifies Baron Samedit among other privesc CVEs.
Another major Linux kernel privesc for older systems.

defense.why_it_works: A heap buffer overflow in sudoedit -s allows overwriting memory structures. By crafting specific environment variables and arguments, an attacker can redirect code execution to gain root privileges.
defense.prerequisites: Any local user account (no sudo permissions needed); vulnerable sudo version.
defense.impact: Instant root privilege escalation from any unprivileged user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068] sudoedit execution with -s flag; crash logs from sudo; unexpected root shell spawning.
defense.artifacts: Sudo segfault in system logs; sudoedit -s in bash history; core dumps from sudo process.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=syslog ("sudoedit" AND "segfault") OR ("sudo" AND "heap" AND "overflow")
| table _time, host, process, message
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "sudoedit" and (SyslogMessage has "segfault" or SyslogMessage has "SIGABRT")
| project TimeGenerated, HostName, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Update sudo to 1.8.32 or 1.9.5p2+; use sudo alternatives; monitor sudoedit usage; apply distro security patches promptly.
